thread:
ashley: heads up — I'm starting an experiment to co-reside two smaller models on a single A100 to cut cost on lower-traffic tenants. hitting some weird perf/regression signals after we tuned the allocator last week. anyone seen this pattern?

raj: saw something similar in perf runs. after allocator pooling changes, tail latency for short seq workloads spiked. p50 looked okay but p95 jumped. :thinking:

marco: can you paste the profiler output? nvprof / nsight summaries help.

ashley: pasted a short summary from a quick run:
```
model-A (gpt-small): p50=18ms p95=54ms mem=6.2GB
model-B (reranker): p50=12ms p95=68ms mem=4.8GB
after allocator pool=enabled + workspace_ratio=0.15
combined p95=110ms, OOM x1 on model-B during burst
```

kai: hmm. sounds like workspace sizing + fragmentation. when we enabled pooling we increased reuse but also introduced larger reserved workspaces that forced different kernel choices (falling back to tiled kernels). kernel selection + workspace size interacts a lot.

olga: +1. in local repro I saw kernel selection flip for attention: small-seq used fused kernel before, now uses generic tiled kernel, ~1.3x slower. That matches p95 bumps.

raj: quick note: our kernel picker is heuristic-based:
```
if seq_len <= 128 and kv_cache_disabled == False:
  prefer = fused_attention_small
elif batch_size >= 8:
  prefer = continuous_batch_attention
else:
  prefer = tiled_attention_large
```
The allocator change added a workspace reservation step which sometimes bumped effective seq_len threshold because of workspace alignment.

marco: also seeing KV cache eviction behavior — when two models share GPU, KV buffers for inactive requests get evicted and then re-populated causing expensive cache warms. profiler shows repeated kv cache allocations and frees.

ashley: thinking of three mitigations: 1) allocator tuning (reduce workspace reservation; favor smaller slab sizes), 2) explicit kernel override for small-seq on co-residency, 3) soft-partition VRAM so each model gets a logical pool and KV cache pinned. thoughts?

kai: for (1) try lowering workspace_ratio to 0.08 and set max_fragmentation_bytes to 16MB. that should force more buffer reuse and keep fused kernels available. for (2) add an override flag `force_kernel=fused_attention_small` per route when model is co-resident. cheap to try.

olga: for (3) soft-partitioning: we can implement per-model allocators (namespaces) with configurable caps. if total mem > cap -> trigger swap or spill-to-host policy. spilling will hurt latency but avoids OOMs.

raj: quick experiment I ran: turned on per-model slab allocator + buffer reuse and got this:
```
before: p95 combined=110ms OOMs/day~6
after: p95 combined=64ms OOMs/day~1 memory_overcommit avoided
```
Throughput stable, slight increase in p50 for model-A (18ms -> 22ms) but p95 much better.

infra-bot: deploy-staging started by ashley — job id: deploy-20240416-72 (will run allocator tweak + kernel override) :rocket:

marco: one more caveat — model swap strategies. swapping entire model weights to host is heavy. better to swap only optimizer-like ephemeral buffers (not during inference) and keep KV caches pinned if SLA requires low latency. for low-tier tenants we can accept swap-to-host during cold periods.

ashley: good point. propose policy matrix:
- SLA-high: reserve KV cache + pin key workspaces, no swapping, dedicated logical pool (cap high)
- SLA-mid: soft-partition, allow KV eviction on LRU, prefer fused kernel override
- SLA-low: aggressive sharing, allow weight swap-to-host and reclaimed workspaces

kai: we should also add a tiny profiler metric: kernel_choice_histogram per model, and workspace_alloc_failures counter. that'll make root-causing quicker.

olga: +1 on metrics. also add an automated smoke that runs co-residency scenario nightly — catch regressions from allocator/kernel changes early.

ashley: ok i'll run the staging job, collect kernel histograms and kv eviction traces, and post results here tomorrow. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: flagging — if staging shows OOM regressions we should pause the allocator rollout. I'll watch alerts during the test.

raj: thanks — if we get stable perf numbers we can bake per-model alloc config into the runtime and ship a default co-residency policy.

ashley: cool. logging outputs and short repro attached to the deploy job. will update thread with numbers.
